Eras.Name: Prehistoric cultures and early settlements (before c. 3500 BCE)
Eras.Features: Early agricultural societies are not all states or civilizations.

Eras.Name: Early Bronze Age (c. 3500–2000 BCE)
Eras.Features: Mesopotamian cities and Nile kingdoms emerge alongside independent Asian developments.

Eras.Name: Middle and Late Bronze Age (c. 2000–1200 BCE)
Eras.Features: Many states coexisted and traded rather than forming a single succession.

Eras.Name: Iron Age and early classical states (c. 1200–500 BCE)
Eras.Features: Israelite and Levantine kingdoms, major empires and city-states.

Eras.Name: Classical and late antique empires (c. 500 BCE–500 CE)
Eras.Features: Separate republican, imperial, regional and dynastic phases.

Eras.Name: Early medieval era (c. 500–1000 CE)
Eras.Features: Contemporaneous Christian, Islamic, African, Asian and American states.

Eras.Name: High and late medieval era (c. 1000–1500 CE)
Eras.Features: A world of kingdoms, sultanates, confederacies, republics and dynasties.

Eras.Name: Early modern / Renaissance to 1700
Eras.Features: Overlapping monarchies, republics, imperial systems and indigenous polities.

Eras.Name: Enlightenment, revolutions and industrial era (c. 1700–1914)
Eras.Features: Modern nations often have predecessor states, changing constitutions and colonial histories.

Eras.Name: 20th-century transitions and contemporary states
Eras.Features: These represent successive political phases, not unique cultures.

Eras.Name: The Fracture Century
Eras.Features: AI logistics, autonomous aircraft, drone fleets, hypersonics, early orbital stations, climate adaptation; regional blocs compete but present states endure.

Eras.Name: The Sky-Lane Age
Eras.Features: Electric vertical-lift skycars, airborne cargo corridors, near-space carriers, defended orbital depots and energy-grid warfare; early off-world settlements.

Eras.Name: The Orbital Sovereignties
Eras.Features: Lunar cities, asteroid manufacturing, orbital fleets, directed-energy point defense, kinetic interceptors and planetary shield infrastructure; Earth–orbit secession wars.

Eras.Name: The Cislunar Wars
Eras.Features: Large space navies, fusion drives as speculative technology, solar power arrays, beam-defense cruisers, autonomous interceptor swarms and contested lunar gateways.

Eras.Name: The Planetary Diasporas
Eras.Features: Independent Mars polities, deep-space habitats, asteroid confederacies, skyborne arcologies, slower interplanetary campaigns and expensive supply wars.

Eras.Name: The Stellar Frontier
Eras.Features: Generation ships, high-endurance robotic armadas, light-limited starflight, exotic speculative propulsion research and sprawling federated worlds.

Eras.Name: The Sovereign Constellations
Eras.Features: Massive dispersed confederacies, self-governing AI cities, solar-system defense architectures, cultural hybridization and unstable imperial alliances.

Eras.Name: The Mythic Machine Age
Eras.Features: Artificial habitats, star-energy infrastructure, heavily fictional gravity manipulation, autonomous fortress worlds and civilization-scale siege campaigns.

Eras.Name: The Fourth Millennium Empires
Eras.Features: Extremely strange successor-state names, interplanetary and interstellar rivalry, colossal defense systems and dynasties whose identities span millennia.

Wars.Name: The First Drone-Treaty Crisis
Wars.Description: Autonomous air fleets challenge old command systems; the crisis ends in uneven international limits and encourages regional defense blocs.

Wars.Name: The Sky-Lane Wars
Wars.Description: Skycars, cargo lifters and airborne defenses are militarized in conflicts over congested megacity air corridors.

Wars.Name: The Battle for the Lunar Gates
Wars.Description: Lunar freighthubs resist Earth-centered control. The first long orbital sieges create autonomous Luna Freeholds.

Wars.Name: The Aquila–Celadon Orbital Wars
Wars.Description: Aquila and East-Asian-descended fleets clash over geostationary infrastructure. Shield grids, kinetic interceptors and beam defense dominate.

Wars.Name: The Three-Planet Crisis
Wars.Description: Earth, Lunar and Martian populations dispute shipping rights. Distant colonies survive by rationing propellant and protecting supply depots.

Wars.Name: The Red Dawn Campaigns
Wars.Description: Martian republics break with old terrestrial institutions. Fusion-powered fleets are powerful but logistics remain decisive.

Wars.Name: The Jarldom Convoy Raids
Wars.Description: Nordic-inspired void jarls use fast boarding craft against asteroid trade routes; convoy coalitions eventually contain them.

Wars.Name: The Spiral Wars
Wars.Description: Star diaspora factions fight for navigational infrastructure. Conflicts are slow across light-year distances and local commanders become semi-independent.

Wars.Name: The Hundred Citadels War
Wars.Description: Fortress habitats and partially autonomous machine fleets contest solar engineering megastructures.

Wars.Name: War of the Broken Constellations
Wars.Description: Long-standing confederations fracture. Citizens on different worlds experience vastly different chronologies due to communications delay.

Wars.Name: The Night of Nine Shields
Wars.Description: Speculative world shields and enormous siege platforms appear in the mythology of a brutal interstellar conflict.

Wars.Name: The Crystal Armada Cataclysm
Wars.Description: Machine-linked fleets overwhelm several stellar crowns before splintering into rival sovereign intelligences.

Wars.Name: The Last Meridian War
Wars.Description: Aquil’Meridian, the Lion Crown and other ancient successors fight over a chain of strategic star systems; exhaustion paves the way for the Grand Concord.
